newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech CNB sets rules on securities exposure.
newsitem.headline: Czech CNB sets rules on securities exposure.

text.p: The Czech National Bank on Thursday said it had set new rules for commercial banks' exposure to losses from securities transactions and property holdings, effective from October 1, but gave no details.
In a brief statement, spokesman Miroslav Kostel said the central bank had also changed rules concerning banks' liquidity, but he did not elaborate.
Central bank officials were not immediately available for further comment.
He said the board had approved "rules on creation of portfolios of securities and shares in property by banks and the coverage of the risks of their loss of value by reserve provisions."
"The aim of this measure is to reduce the market risk emerging from the trading in securities and shares in property," Kostel added.
Although he did not say what the regualtions would be, it would apply to all Czech banks and branches of foreign banks operating in the Czech Republic from October 1.
The country has been stung by a handful of failures of small and medium-sized banks reportedly due in part to losses from the financing of risky securities transactions.
Kostel said another measure had been passed, effective on January 1, which would alter the rules of liquidity of banks.
